This tiny mass places the newborn pups among the smallest offspring relative to adult size within the Heteromyidae family. The in utero embryo undergoes rapid organogenesis during this window, culminating in the delivery of pups that, despite their low initial mass, are sufficiently developed to begin suckling almost immediately after the birth event.

Following parturition, the suckling juvenile stage is characterized by an intense period of nursing and growth. The pups remain sequestered in the subterranean nest for several weeks, during which time they undergo a pronounced increase in body mass. The wet weight at weaning, the point at which the young begin to consume solid food independently, is 28.1 grams [Wwx = 28.1 grams]. The nutritional independence gained at this stage initiates a period of rapid somatic growth towards the adult body plan.

As the weaned juveniles continue their development, they progress through a sub-adult phase before attaining full reproductive competence. The ultimate wet weight for a fully grown adult Heermann's kangaroo rat is approximately 65 grams [Wwi = approximately 65 grams], a mass that places it in the intermediate size range among its congeners.
